methods.name: block.close
methods.description: Close a block and end the program running in it.

session_id.description: The session that holds the block.

block_id.description: The block to close. It may be a detached block. Send this or window_id, not both.

window_id.description: The window whose focused block to close. It doesn't have to be the active window. Send this or block_id, not both.

keep_last.description: If true, fail rather than close the only block left in a window, counting floating layers. Ignored for detached blocks.

block_id.description: The block that closed.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the block was detached, because a detached block isn't part of the view.

session_id.description: The session that holds the block.

block_id.description: The block to send the event to.

type.description: The kind of event, such as key, paste, mouse, wheel, or focus.

payload.description: The event's fields. Leaving it out is the same as an empty object.

event.description: The event to send: its type, such as paste, and its payload.

methods.name: block.method

session_id.description: The session that holds the block.

block_id.description: The block to call the method on.

method.description: The block method's short name, such as write or format.

args.description: The block method's own arguments. Leaving it out is the same as an empty object.

title.description: A short name for people to read, such as Terminal.

description.description: A sentence about what the creator's blocks do.

title.description: A short name for people to read, such as Shell.

description.description: A sentence about what this flavor creates.

options_schema.description: A JSON Schema for the options this flavor accepts.

events.description: The block events, by name. Each value is a JSON Schema for the event's fields.

methods.description: The block methods, by short name.

input_schema.description: A JSON Schema for the method's arguments.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema for the method's result.

name.description: The action's short name, such as reset. Its full name, used in key bindings, is the creator's name, a dot, and this name.

title.description: The name to show a person, such as Reset Terminal.

description.description: A sentence about what the action does, to show under its title in a menu or command palette.

category.description: A group of related actions, such as Pane.

keywords.description: More words to search for the action by, separated by spaces.

args.description: The fixed arguments the method is called with when the action runs. Left out when there are none.

repeats.description: True if holding the key down should run the action again, as holding an arrow key does.

actions.description: The actions that call this method, in the order the creator declares them.

api.description: The methods and events that this creator's blocks provide.

features.description: Optional features the creator supports. Ignore names you don't know. No names are defined yet.

creators.description: Every creator available, with its flavors and the API its blocks provide.

methods.name: client.action

action.description: The full name of the action, such as dev_layout or com.superlogical.terminal.reset. client.keymap lists them.

args.description: The action's arguments, as a JSON object. Leave it out if there are none, and always for an action a creator declares.

origin.description: What caused the request: key, palette, or api (the default). The action reads it as ctx.origin. Other values count as api, but script makes the call fail with bad_request.

session_id.description: The session the action applies to. Required for a block action. A configuration file action may leave it out, and then has no default session.

block_id.description: The block the action applies to. Defaults to the session's focused block, unless server is set. Requires session_id.

name.description: The name an action uses for the server, in rex.server(name) and ctx.server. It must be unique and not empty.

id.description: Any non-empty value the client uses to recognize the server. It comes back unchanged in client_call_requested events.

servers.description: Other servers this client is connected to, which a configuration file action can call with rex.server(name). Don't list the server you're sending this to.

action.description: The name of the client action to perform. Ignore a name you don't know.

args.description: The action's arguments, as a JSON object. Left out if there are none.

client_actions.description: Actions the configuration file action asked this client to perform with rex.client.queue, in order. Perform each one as you would a key binding.

ordered_after.description: The id of the request this connection ran just before this one, counting only methods that run in order, such as client.key. Left out if there was none.

methods.name: client.inspect

client_id.description: The client to describe. It can be any client, not only the one calling.

name.description: The program's name, such as Rex.app or rex. If it is longer than 256 bytes, the server keeps only the first 256.

version.description: The program's version, as the program prints it, such as 1.6.0. If it is longer than 256 bytes, the server keeps only the first 256.

label.description: The client's label, such as studio. Two clients can share a label.

info.description: What the client says about itself, such as its name and version, for showing to people. Left out if it said nothing.

transport.description: How the client first reached Rex: 'unix', 'named_pipe', 'tcp', or 'tailscale'. A login server passes it on unchanged.

display.description: A readable name for the client, such as uid 501 or alice@example.com. It can be out of date or shared, so compare uid, sid, or user_id instead.

remote_addr.description: The client's network address. Left out when there is none, such as on a Unix socket.

uid.description: The client's Unix user ID. Only for kind peer.

gid.description: The client's Unix group ID. Only for kind peer.

pid.description: The client's process ID when it connected, for kind peer or windows_peer, if known. Process IDs are reused, so use it only for debugging.

sid.description: The client's Windows security identifier, which survives account renames. Only for kind windows_peer.

user_id.description: The Tailscale user ID that owns the client's device. Only for kind tailscale. Check tags before treating it as a person.

login_name.description: The client's Tailscale login name, usually an email address. For display only.

node.description: The name of the client's Tailscale device. Only for kind tailscale.

tags.description: The Tailscale tags of the client's device. Any tag means the client is a machine, such as a CI runner, not a person.

path.description: The route the client took to this server, for troubleshooting. Entries include 'tailscale' (built-in Tailscale), 'tailnet' and 'tailnet-serve' (the machine's own Tailscale), and 'login-server' (passed on by a login server).

principal.description: Who the client is, as the server identified it when it accepted the connection.

connected_at.description: When the client first connected, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. It doesn't change when the client reconnects.

connection_state.description: Whether the client has a connection: connected, or lost if it dropped and the client may still reconnect. Treat a missing or unknown value as connected.

connection_lost_at.description: When the server noticed the connection drop, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Set only while connection_state is lost.

session_ids.description: The sessions the client attached to with session.attach or session.bootstrap, sorted by ID. Left out if there are none.

client.description: The client, as client.list describes it.

name.description: The name that bindings use for the action, such as pane.split. Names from the configuration file never contain a dot.

kind.description: What performs the action: client (the client itself), lua (a rex.action in the configuration file), or block (a block of the creator that the name starts with).

title.description: The name to show a person, such as Split Pane.

description.description: A sentence about what the action does, to show under its title in a menu or command palette.

category.description: A group of related actions, such as Layouts. Configuration file actions without one are filed under Actions.

keywords.description: More words to search for the action by, separated by spaces.

args.description: A JSON Schema of the arguments the action takes. Left out when the action doesn't describe any.

repeats.description: True if holding the key down should run the action again, as holding an arrow key does.

source.description: Where the action is defined, as file:line, such as init.lua:12. Left out when there's no location, as for every action a client declares.

actions.description: The actions the client declared in its latest client.keymap request that listed any. Left out if it declared none.

methods.name: client.key
methods.description: Send a key to a block, giving Lua key bindings the first chance at it.

session_id.description: The session the key is typed in.

key.description: The physical key, named after its W3C KeyboardEvent code in snake_case, such as key_a for KeyA, the A key on a US keyboard. It doesn't change with the keyboard layout. Any other key is unidentified.

mods.description: The modifier keys held down, joined with + in this order: shift, ctrl, alt, super, caps_lock, num_lock, shift_side, ctrl_side, alt_side, super_side. On a Mac, super is the Command key. The lock names mean the lock is on, and a name ending in _side means the right-hand key of that pair is held. An empty string means none.

consumed_mods.description: The modifiers the keyboard layout used to produce text, such as shift for a capital letter. Written like mods, which also includes them.

text.description: The text the key typed. Empty for keys that type nothing, such as arrows and modifiers.

unshifted_codepoint.description: The Unicode code point the key types without shift, such as 110 for n. Bindings such as ctrl+n match on it, so they follow the keyboard layout. 0 if none.

composing.description: True while the key is part of an unfinished composition, such as a dead key or an input method.

action.description: What happened to the key: press, release, or repeat while it's held down.

key.description: The key event, as the keyboard reported it.

block_id.description: The block to send the key to. Defaults to the session's focused block.

prefix.description: The keys pressed before key when key ends a key sequence, in order. For ctrl+b then x, send x as key and ctrl+b here.

handled.description: True if a Lua function in the client's script or the configuration file took the key. No block received it then.

methods.name: client.keymap
methods.description: Get what each key does for this client. The result combines the client's own bindings with the configuration file and the client's Lua scripts.

name.description: The name that bindings use for the action, such as pane.split. Names from the configuration file never contain a dot.

kind.description: What performs the action: client (the client itself), lua (a rex.action in the configuration file), or block (a block of the creator that the name starts with).

args.description: A JSON Schema of the arguments the action takes. Left out when the action doesn't describe any.

repeats.description: True if holding the key down should run the action again, as holding an arrow key does.

source.description: Where the action is defined, as file:line, such as init.lua:12. Left out when there's no location, as for every action a client declares.

actions.description: The actions the client performs itself. Leave it out to skip the checks for unknown actions and wrong arguments. The server keeps the list for client.inspect and client.perform.

server_actions.description: Which of the server's actions the reply lists: all (the default), configured (only the configuration file's), or none. An unknown value means all.

name.description: The layer's name, such as default or settings, which its bindings report as their source. Unique in the request, with no colon.

keys.description: The keys that trigger the binding, such as cmd+k, or cmd+[KeyK] for a key by its position. A key sequence has one element per key, in the order pressed.

action.description: The name of the action to run.

args.description: The arguments to run the action with, as a JSON object, exactly as the user wrote them. Left out if there are none.

source.description: Where the binding came from: a layer name, such as default, or a file:line, such as init.lua:12. Ignored in a request.

mode.description: The mode the binding belongs to, such as resize. The binding applies only while that mode is active. Left out for a binding outside every mode.

bindings.description: What the layer binds, in the order it bound them. A later binding sits above an earlier one on the same key.

keys.description: The keys to clear, spelled like a binding's keys. Only the same spelling matches. Empty, with mode set, to remove that whole mode.

action.description: The one action to take off the keys, such as pane.split. Leave it out to clear the keys whatever is bound to them.

mode.description: The mode to remove the keys from. Leave it out for keys outside every mode. With empty keys, it removes the whole mode.

removals.description: What the layer takes off the layers beneath it. Removals never touch the layer's own bindings.

defaults.description: The client's built-in layers, lowest first. They sit beneath the configuration file. Problems found only in them aren't reported, because the user can't edit them.

name.description: The layer's name, such as default or settings, which its bindings report as their source. Unique in the request, with no colon.

mode.description: The mode to remove the keys from. Leave it out for keys outside every mode. With empty keys, it removes the whole mode.

removals.description: What the layer takes off the layers beneath it. Removals never touch the layer's own bindings.

overrides.description: Layers of shortcuts a person recorded in the client, lowest first. They sit above the configuration file and this client's scripts. Problems in them come back as warnings.

args.description: The arguments to run the action with, as a JSON object, exactly as the user wrote them. Left out if there are none.

message.description: The problem in one sentence, ready to show. Its wording may change, so don't parse it.

action.description: The full name of the action the problem is about, as written, even if misspelled. Left out if it isn't about one action.

key.description: The key the problem is about, spelled like a binding's keys, with a sequence joined by spaces, such as ctrl+a b. Left out if it isn't about one key.

mode.description: The mode the problem is about. Left out if it isn't about a mode.

actions.description: The server's actions that keys can be bound to: the configuration file's, then each creator's, by creator name. Left out when there are none.

name.description: The mode's name, such as resize. Its bindings have it as their mode, and client.mode.enter takes it as its name argument.

exclusive.description: True if keys the mode doesn't bind are ignored while it's active. If false, they do what they do outside the mode.

blocked.description: Keys that must not reach the bindings outside the mode while it's active. If the mode also binds one, that binding still runs. Each is spelled like a binding's keys.

methods.name: client.perform
methods.description: Ask another client to perform one of its actions and wait for its answer.

client_id.description: The client to ask. To find one by its label, call target.resolve with kinds set to client.

action.description: The name of an action the client declared, such as pane.split. client.inspect lists them. At most 256 bytes.

args.description: The action's arguments, as a JSON object. Leave it out if there are none.

origin.description: What caused the request, such as key, palette, api, or cli. The client receives it unchanged. Empty means api.

session_id.description: The session the action applies to, if any. The client receives it without the server checking it.

block_id.description: The block to act on instead of the client's focused block, if any. The client receives it without the server checking it.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the answer, in milliseconds, once the client is sent the request. Defaults to 10000. Values over 30000 count as 30000.

result.description: What the client's action returned. Left out if it returned null, as most actions do.

performed_by.description: The client that performed the action. It is always the client that client_id named.

methods.name: client.reply
methods.description: Answer a client_call_requested, client_perform_requested, or client_prompt_requested event.

call_id.description: The call_id of the event you're answering.

result.description: The call's result, what the action returned, or the prompt's answer. For a call or action with no output, use null. For a prompt, send a prompt result: text, ids, or cancelled. Set this or error, not both.

code.description: The kind of failure, as an error code such as not_found, refused, or internal.

message.description: What went wrong, written for people. In client.reply, a message longer than 4096 bytes is shortened and ends with an ellipsis.

error.description: Why the call failed, the action wasn't performed, or the prompt couldn't be shown. Set this or result, not both.

methods.name: client.set_label
methods.description: Set or remove this client's label.

label.description: The label to set, such as studio. An empty string removes it. At most 64 bytes, with no control characters.

methods.name: client.set_script
methods.description: Load Lua scripts for this client, replacing any it loaded before.

name.description: A file name to show in error messages and diagnostics, such as init.lua.

scripts.description: Every Lua source to load, run in order. They replace all the scripts loaded before. An empty list unloads them.

items.description: A key binding: modifiers, then a key, joined with +, such as ctrl+n or cmd+left. The modifiers are ctrl, alt, shift, and cmd, always in that order. bindings.description: The single keys the scripts bind to Lua functions. A key sent alone reaches the scripts only if it's listed here and pressed or repeating. Key sequences aren't listed.

all_keys.description: Never sent by this server. If an older server sends true, send every key to client.key, not only those in bindings.

methods.name: data.connect
methods.description: Get a one-time ticket for opening a data connection to a block. A data connection streams a block's content as it changes, such as a terminal's output.

session_id.description: The session that holds the block. The connection must be attached to it with session.attach or session.bootstrap.

block_id.description: The block that provides the data.

data_ref_id.description: Which of the block's data sources to open, such as terminal.

subprotocol.description: The subprotocol the data connection will use, such as rex.data.terminal.v1. If set, the ticket works only on a connection that uses it.

ticket.description: A single-use ticket to send in the HELLO message that opens the data connection. Only a data connection from the same user can use it.

expires_in_ms.description: How long the ticket stays valid after the server issues it, in milliseconds.

methods.name: help.all
methods.description: Describe every method the server provides, including block methods.

methods.name: hosts.list
methods.description: List the server's hosts: the other Rex servers you connect to by label.

id.description: The host's ID, such as host:<uuid>, chosen by the device that adds the host. If hosts.put leaves it out, the server creates one.

label.description: The name you connect to the host by, such as studio. Unique in the list, ignoring case, and at most 64 characters.

endpoints.description: The addresses that reach the host, in the order to try them, such as studio.tail1234.ts.net or unix:///tmp/rex.sock. Each takes a form the -S option of rex accepts. A socket path works only on a device where the path exists, such as the local end of an ssh -L forward.

icon.description: The name of an icon for clients to show next to the label. Rex doesn't interpret it.

host_id.description: The host_id that the host's server.status reported when the host was added, if known. Compare it with a server's host_id to tell whether this host is that server.

kind.description: How the server identified the client: 'peer' (Unix socket credentials), 'windows_peer' (named pipe credentials), 'tailscale' (a Tailscale login), or 'anonymous' (not identified). Show a kind you don't know by its name.

transport.description: How the client first reached Rex: 'unix', 'named_pipe', 'tcp', or 'tailscale'. A login server passes it on unchanged.

display.description: A readable name for the client, such as uid 501 or alice@example.com. It can be out of date or shared, so compare uid, sid, or user_id instead.

remote_addr.description: The client's network address. Left out when there is none, such as on a Unix socket.

uid.description: The client's Unix user ID. Only for kind peer.

gid.description: The client's Unix group ID. Only for kind peer.

pid.description: The client's process ID when it connected, for kind peer or windows_peer, if known. Process IDs are reused, so use it only for debugging.

sid.description: The client's Windows security identifier, which survives account renames. Only for kind windows_peer.

user_id.description: The Tailscale user ID that owns the client's device. Only for kind tailscale. Check tags before treating it as a person.

login_name.description: The client's Tailscale login name, usually an email address. For display only.

node.description: The name of the client's Tailscale device. Only for kind tailscale.

tags.description: The Tailscale tags of the client's device. Any tag means the client is a machine, such as a CI runner, not a person.

path.description: The route the client took to this server, for troubleshooting. Entries include 'tailscale' (built-in Tailscale), 'tailnet' and 'tailnet-serve' (the machine's own Tailscale), and 'login-server' (passed on by a login server).

principal.description: How the server identified you when your connection opened.

account.description: The operating system account the server runs as. It can differ from your own name. Left out when unknown.

methods.name: session.attach
methods.description: Attach to a session: start receiving its events and get its current view.

client_id.description: This connection's client ID. It's the same for every session the connection attaches to.

revision.description: The view's revision. A larger revision is a newer view of the session, even across a server restart. It goes up by one with each change, and jumps ahead when a restarted server restores the session.

active_window_id.description: The window the session shows. Left out when the session has no windows.

focused_block_id.description: The window's focused block, which receives typing while the window is active. Left out if the window has none.

zoomed_block_id.description: The block zoomed to fill the window, if any. Layouts keep their normal sizes, so draw this block over the whole window.

kind.description: How the layer is placed: 'tiled' for the layer that fills the window, or 'floating' for a floating layer. Draw a kind you don't know as 'floating'.

bounds.description: Where the layer sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height.

state.description: How the layer is presented: 'minimized' means don't draw it, though its blocks keep running, and only a floating layer can be minimized. Left out for a normal layer. Draw a state you don't know as normal.

rect.description: Where this node sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height.

block_id.description: The block at this node. Set only when split isn't.

split_id.description: The split's ID. It stays the same while the split exists, so you can match splits across views.

direction.description: How the space is divided: 'horizontal' puts before on the left and after on the right, and 'vertical' puts before above after. Draw a direction you don't know as 'horizontal'.

ratio.description: The fraction of the space that before gets, between 0 and 1.

before.description: The node on the left or top.

after.description: The node on the right or bottom.

split.description: How this node divides in two. Set only when block_id isn't.

layout.description: How the layer divides its space between blocks, as a tree of splits. Null when the layer is empty.

block_id.description: The block's ID.

creator_name.description: The creator that made the block, such as com.superlogical.terminal.

flavor.description: The flavor the block was made from, such as com.superlogical.terminal.shell.

host_id.description: Identifies the machine and account the block runs as. If it equals your local server's host_id, the block sees the same files you do. Otherwise treat the block as remote.

owner.description: The client that owns the block. Left out when the block has no owner.

blocks.description: The blocks in the layer, in layout order. The layout field says where each one sits.

layers.description: The window's layers, from back to front. The first is the tiled layer, which holds the window's layout and fills the window.

windows.description: The session's windows, in order. Rex.app shows them as tabs in this order.

view.description: The session's view, read after the connection started receiving its events. Apply it first, then the events whose seq is higher than the response's.

event_scope.description: Which events to receive. 'session' sends every session's events except block_event, plus session_created, session_destroyed, session_moved, and tailscale_status_changed. 'all' also sends block_event and the client events, such as client_joined.

sessions.description: Every session on the server when this connection started receiving events.

tailnet_name.description: The tailnet's display name, or its domain if it has none. Left out until known.

tags.description: The Tailscale tags the device has, such as tag:rex. A tagged device has no owner. Left out when it has none.

mode.description: How to claim them. 'take' makes the calling client the owner right away. 'request' makes it the owner only of blocks that have none, and it may get the rest when their owner gives them up or leaves. Defaults to take.

block_id.description: The block's ID.

owner.description: The client that owns the block. Left out when the block has no owner.

blocks.description: Each claimed block and its owner after this call.

methods.name: session.raise_layer
methods.description: Move a floating layer to the front, or just above another floating layer.

layer_id.description: The floating layer to move forward.

relative_layer_id.description: Another floating layer in the same window to place it just above. Leave it out to move it in front of every other floating layer.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

methods.name: session.resize_layer
methods.description: Move or resize a floating layer.

layer_id.description: The floating layer to move or resize.

bounds.description: The layer's new position and size, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height. It must fit inside the window.

anyOf.description: A rectangle as [x, y, w, h]. x and y place its top-left corner and w and h give its size, each as a fraction of the window's width or height.

x.description: The left edge, as a fraction of the window's width.

y.description: The top edge, as a fraction of the window's height.

w.description: The width, as a fraction of the window's width.

h.description: The height, as a fraction of the window's height.

anyOf.description: The same rectangle as an object, the form that earlier clients send.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

methods.name: session.resize_pane
methods.description: Move the border between two blocks to change their sizes.

direction.description: The kind of split between the two blocks: 'horizontal' for a border between left and right, or 'vertical' for one between top and bottom.

before_block_id.description: A block on the left of the border, or above it when direction is vertical.

after_block_id.description: A block on the right of the border, or below it when direction is vertical.

ratio.description: The fraction of the split's space that the before part gets, greater than 0 and less than 1.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

methods.name: session.set_block_label
methods.description: Set a block's label.

block_id.description: The block to relabel. Required.

label.description: The new label, up to 128 characters. An empty or missing label restores a default made from the block's ID.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

methods.name: session.set_label
methods.description: Set the session's label.

label.description: The new label, up to 128 characters. An empty or missing label restores the label the server chose when it created the session.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

methods.name: session.set_layer_state
methods.description: Minimize a floating layer or return it to normal, optionally raising and focusing it.

state.description: The state to set: 'normal' or 'minimized'.

focus.description: Whether to also raise the layer, focus the block last focused in it, and make its window active, all in one change. Needs state to be 'normal' and the layer to have a block. Defaults to false.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

methods.name: session.set_window_label
methods.description: Set a window's label.

label.description: The new label, up to 128 characters. An empty or missing label restores a default made from the window's ID.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

methods.name: session.swap_blocks
methods.description: Swap the places of two blocks.

block_id.description: One of the two blocks to swap.

other_block_id.description: The other block. The order of the two doesn't matter.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows, unless the method's notes say otherwise.

methods.name: session.view
methods.description: Get the session's windows, their layouts, and their blocks in one snapshot.

revision.description: The view's revision. A larger revision is a newer view of the session, even across a server restart. It goes up by one with each change, and jumps ahead when a restarted server restores the session.

active_window_id.description: The window the session shows. Left out when the session has no windows.

focused_block_id.description: The window's focused block, which receives typing while the window is active. Left out if the window has none.

zoomed_block_id.description: The block zoomed to fill the window, if any. Layouts keep their normal sizes, so draw this block over the whole window.

kind.description: How the layer is placed: 'tiled' for the layer that fills the window, or 'floating' for a floating layer. Draw a kind you don't know as 'floating'.

bounds.description: Where the layer sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height.

state.description: How the layer is presented: 'minimized' means don't draw it, though its blocks keep running, and only a floating layer can be minimized. Left out for a normal layer. Draw a state you don't know as normal.

rect.description: Where this node sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height.

block_id.description: The block at this node. Set only when split isn't.

split_id.description: The split's ID. It stays the same while the split exists, so you can match splits across views.

direction.description: How the space is divided: 'horizontal' puts before on the left and after on the right, and 'vertical' puts before above after. Draw a direction you don't know as 'horizontal'.

ratio.description: The fraction of the space that before gets, between 0 and 1.

before.description: The node on the left or top.

after.description: The node on the right or bottom.

split.description: How this node divides in two. Set only when block_id isn't.

layout.description: How the layer divides its space between blocks, as a tree of splits. Null when the layer is empty.

block_id.description: The block's ID.

creator_name.description: The creator that made the block, such as com.superlogical.terminal.

flavor.description: The flavor the block was made from, such as com.superlogical.terminal.shell.

host_id.description: Identifies the machine and account the block runs as. If it equals your local server's host_id, the block sees the same files you do. Otherwise treat the block as remote.

owner.description: The client that owns the block. Left out when the block has no owner.

blocks.description: The blocks in the layer, in layout order. The layout field says where each one sits.

layers.description: The window's layers, from back to front. The first is the tiled layer, which holds the window's layout and fills the window.

windows.description: The session's windows, in order. Rex.app shows them as tabs in this order.

methods.name: session.zoom_block
methods.description: Zoom a block to fill its window, or undo the zoom.

block_id.description: The block to zoom. It takes focus, and its window becomes active. Leave it out to use the focused block of window_id, or of the active window.

window_id.description: A window whose focused block to zoom. The active window doesn't change. Send it only when block_id is left out.

zoom.description: Set true to zoom or false to restore the layout. Leave it out to switch between the two.

block_id.description: The block this call zoomed or restored. If the request didn't name one, this is the focused block the server used.

zoomed.description: Whether the block is zoomed after this call.

revision.description: The session's revision after this call. It is unchanged if the call changed nothing that session.view shows.

methods.name: target.complete
methods.description: List the labels, window positions, and short IDs that start with a prefix. Use it to complete a name as someone types it.

kinds.description: What to complete: session, window, block, or client, with the same rules as in target.resolve. Completions come back in this order.

prefix.description: The text typed so far. It matches the start of labels (ignoring case), window positions, and short IDs. An empty prefix matches everything.

session_id.description: The caller's session. Without scope.session, windows and blocks are searched only in this session, and an empty session query selects it.

block_id.description: The caller's block, such as the terminal a script runs in. In target.resolve, empty block and window queries default to it and its window.

client_id.description: The caller's own client. In target.resolve, an empty client query selects it if it's among the clients searched.

context.description: Where the caller is. Only session_id is used: without scope.session, windows and blocks come from that session.

session.description: The session to search in, named by ID, label, or the end of its ID. A client search then covers only clients attached to it.

window.description: The window to search in, named by ID, label, position, or the end of its ID. Allowed only when kinds is just block.

scope.description: Limits completion to one session, or block completion to one window, as in target.resolve.

value.description: The text to offer, such as a label, a window position, or a short ID.

form.description: What value is: 'label', 'ordinal' (a window position), or 'id' (a short ID, the last six hexadecimal digits of an ID).

kind.description: What this is: session, window, block, or client. Skip a candidate whose kind you don't know.

session_id.description: The session's ID, or the ID of the session that holds the window or block. Left out for a client.

window_id.description: The window's ID, or the ID of the window that holds the block. Left out for sessions, clients, and detached blocks.

block_id.description: The block's ID. Set only for blocks.

client_id.description: The client's ID. Set only for clients.

label.description: Its label, or an empty string if it has none.

ordinal.description: A window's position in its session, counting from 1, in the order session.view lists windows. Left out for everything else.

where.description: Where it is, for showing to a person, such as 'window 2' or 'detached'. For a client, the program, such as 'Rex.app 1.6.0'. May be empty. Don't parse it.

target.description: The session, window, block, or client that value names.

completions.description: Every match, grouped by kind in the order of kinds. Empty if nothing matches or a scope doesn't resolve.

methods.name: target.resolve
methods.description: Look up sessions, windows, blocks, or clients by ID, label, or position. Each query gets its own result, which says whether it matched one thing, nothing, or several.

kinds.description: What each query may name: session, window, block, or client. List each kind once, and list client only on its own.

queries.description: The names to look up. Each is a full ID, a label, a window position, the end of an ID, or an empty string for the default.

session_id.description: The caller's session. Without scope.session, windows and blocks are searched only in this session, and an empty session query selects it.

block_id.description: The caller's block, such as the terminal a script runs in. In target.resolve, empty block and window queries default to it and its window.

client_id.description: The caller's own client. In target.resolve, an empty client query selects it if it's among the clients searched.

context.description: Where the caller is, such as the terminal a script runs in. IDs in it that no longer exist are ignored.

session.description: The session to search in, named by ID, label, or the end of its ID. A client search then covers only clients attached to it.

window.description: The window to search in, named by ID, label, position, or the end of its ID. Allowed only when kinds is just block.

scope.description: Limits the search to one session, or a block search to one window. Not allowed when kinds includes session.

query.description: The query this result answers, exactly as sent.

status.description: Whether the query matched: 'resolved' for one thing, 'not_found' for nothing, or 'ambiguous' for several. Treat a value you don't know as 'not_found'.

kind.description: What this is: session, window, block, or client. Skip a candidate whose kind you don't know.

session_id.description: The session's ID, or the ID of the session that holds the window or block. Left out for a client.

window_id.description: The window's ID, or the ID of the window that holds the block. Left out for sessions, clients, and detached blocks.

block_id.description: The block's ID. Set only for blocks.

client_id.description: The client's ID. Set only for clients.

label.description: Its label, or an empty string if it has none.

ordinal.description: A window's position in its session, counting from 1, in the order session.view lists windows. Left out for everything else.

where.description: Where it is, for showing to a person, such as 'window 2' or 'detached'. For a client, the program, such as 'Rex.app 1.6.0'. May be empty. Don't parse it.

target.description: What the query matched. Set only when status is resolved.

reason.description: Why the query didn't resolve, for showing to a person. May be empty.

kind.description: What this is: session, window, block, or client. Skip a candidate whose kind you don't know.

session_id.description: The session's ID, or the ID of the session that holds the window or block. Left out for a client.

window_id.description: The window's ID, or the ID of the window that holds the block. Left out for sessions, clients, and detached blocks.

block_id.description: The block's ID. Set only for blocks.

client_id.description: The client's ID. Set only for clients.

label.description: Its label, or an empty string if it has none.

ordinal.description: A window's position in its session, counting from 1, in the order session.view lists windows. Left out for everything else.

where.description: Where it is, for showing to a person, such as 'window 2' or 'detached'. For a client, the program, such as 'Rex.app 1.6.0'. May be empty. Don't parse it.

candidates.description: When status is ambiguous, the choices for a person to pick from. Check each one's kind.

results.description: One result for each query, in the same order as queries.

methods.name: set_step
methods.description: Move the walkthrough to another step. Emits step_changed when the step changes.

step.description: The step to move to. Empty means the first step.

generation.description: Increases with every change to the state.

step.description: The step the walkthrough is on. Empty means the first step.

methods.name: state
methods.description: Return the step the walkthrough is on.

generation.description: Increases with every change to the state.

step.description: The step the walkthrough is on. Empty means the first step.

methods.name: blob_read
methods.description: Read a result that was too large for one reply or event, such as the output of format with max_bytes set, or a selection_copied event without text. The server keeps each result for about five minutes.

id.description: The result to read, from the reply or event that named it, such as the id in a format reply or a selection_copied event. Zero or left out reads the newest result, whatever produced it. If the server no longer has the result, the call fails with not_found.

offset.description: Where to start reading, in bytes from the start of the result. To read the next part, add the length in bytes of the data you received. Must not be negative.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of data to return, measured once it is encoded as a JSON string. Zero or left out means 49152 (48 KiB), and values above 983040 (960 KiB) are lowered to that. Must not be negative.

id.description: The result that was read. Send it in later requests so that every part comes from the same result.

data.description: The text read, starting at offset. It never ends partway through a character. It can be shorter than max_bytes even when more text remains.

total.description: The length of the whole result, in bytes.

eof.description: True if data reaches the end of the result.

methods.name: clear
methods.description: Clear the screen and scrollback, keeping the current line at the top. It changes nothing while a full-screen program, such as an editor, is running.

methods.name: clipboard_read
methods.description: Read text that a program in the terminal copied to the clipboard. The server keeps each copy for about a minute, so a client can read text too large to send in an event.

id.description: The copy to read, from a clipboard_written event or an earlier reply. Zero or left out reads the newest copy. If the server no longer has the copy, the call fails with not_found.

offset.description: Where to start reading, in bytes from the start of the text. To read the next part, add the length in bytes of the data you received. Must not be negative.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of data to return, measured once it is encoded as a JSON string. Zero or left out means 49152 (48 KiB), and values above 983040 (960 KiB) are lowered to that. Must not be negative.

id.description: The copy that was read. Send it in later requests so that every part comes from the same copy.

data.description: The text read, starting at offset. It never ends partway through a character. It can be shorter than max_bytes even when more text remains.

total.description: The length of the whole copied text, in bytes.

eof.description: True if data reaches the end of the text.

methods.name: download_begin
methods.description: Open a file on the terminal's machine for download, and get a ticket for the rex.data.bytes.v1 data stream that carries its bytes from the terminal. A relative path is relative to the working directory of the terminal's foreground process. Only regular files can be downloaded.

ref.description: The data reference for the file's stream: download: followed by a new UUID in lower-case canonical form, which the client chooses.

path.description: The file to download. A relative path is relative to the working directory of the terminal's foreground process, and a leading ~ is the home directory.

if_none_match.description: The version of the copy the client already has, from an earlier result for the same path. If the file still has it, the result has not_modified and no ticket.

ticket.description: A single-use ticket to send in the HELLO message that opens the data connection. Only a data connection from the same user can use it. Left out with not_modified.

expires_in_ms.description: How long the ticket stays valid after the server issues it, in milliseconds. Left out with not_modified.

not_modified.description: The file still has the version named in if_none_match, so the client's copy is current. There is no ticket and nothing to download.

path.description: The absolute path of the file, with symlinks left as they are.

name.description: The file's name: the last element of path.

size.description: The file's size in bytes when it was opened, for showing progress only. The stream may carry more or fewer bytes if the file changes.

modified_at.description: The file's modification time when it was opened, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Programs can set it to anything, so use version to tell whether the file changed.

version.description: An opaque string that changes whenever the file's contents may have, for caching. The same path with the same version has the same contents. Left out when the file changed within the last second, or when the server can't tell, and then the download must not be cached.

methods.name: format
methods.description: Get the screen and scrollback as plain text, HTML, or escape sequences.

format.description: The format to return: 'text' for plain text, 'html' for HTML with inline styles, or 'vt' for escape sequences that redraw the screen with its colors and styles. Defaults to 'text'.

trim.description: Remove spaces from the end of each line.

unwrap.description: Join lines that the terminal wrapped because they were too long, so each line of output is one line the program wrote.

extra_charsets.description: Include the selected character sets. Only used with the vt format.

extra_cursor.description: Include the cursor position. Only used with the vt format.

extra_hyperlink.description: Include the hyperlink in effect at the cursor. Only used with the vt format.

extra_keyboard.description: Include keyboard modes such as modifyOtherKeys. Only used with the vt format.

extra_kitty_keyboard.description: Include the state of the Kitty keyboard protocol. Only used with the vt format.

extra_modes.description: Include terminal modes that differ from their defaults. Only used with the vt format.

extra_palette.description: Include the color palette. Only used with the vt format.

extra_protection.description: Include the character protection mode. Only used with the vt format.

extra_pwd.description: Include the reported working directory. Only used with the vt format.

extra_scrolling_region.description: Include the scrolling region. Only used with the vt format.

extra_style.description: Include the text style in effect at the cursor. Only used with the vt format.

extra_tabstops.description: Include the tab stops. Only used with the vt format.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of content to return, measured once it is encoded as a JSON string. If more output remains, the reply has an id, and you read the rest with blob_read. Values above 983040 (960 KiB) are lowered to that. Zero or left out returns the whole output in one reply, and the call fails with too_large if the output doesn't fit. Must not be negative.

content.description: The screen and scrollback in the requested format. If id is set, this is only the first part.

id.description: Set only when more output remains. To read the rest, call blob_read with this id and with offset set to the length of content in bytes. A reply without id holds the whole output.

total.description: The length of the whole output in bytes. Sent only when the request set max_bytes, and left out when it is 0.

eof.description: True if content is the whole output. Sent only when the request set max_bytes. Older servers never send it, so check id instead to tell whether more output remains.

methods.name: input_mode
methods.description: Get how the terminal handles typed input, such as whether it is echoed. On Windows the call fails with not_found.

echo.description: True if typed characters appear on the screen. A program usually turns this off while it reads a password.

canonical.description: True if input reaches the program a line at a time, with backspace and similar keys handled before the program sees it.

signals.description: True if keys such as Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Z send signals to the foreground process instead of reaching it as input.

methods.name: list_dir
methods.description: List the subdirectories of a directory, and optionally its files. A relative path or ~ is resolved the way a program in the terminal would resolve it.

path.description: The directory to list: an absolute path, ~ or a path under ~/ for the home directory, or a path relative to the working directory of the terminal's foreground process. Empty lists that working directory.

prefix.description: Keep only entries whose names start with this text, ignoring case. Use it to narrow a listing that came back truncated.

limit.description: The most entries to return. Zero, negative, or left out means 2000.

files.description: Include entries that aren't directories, such as files, and mark each with file set to true.

path.description: The directory that was listed, as an absolute path. It is set even when the directory couldn't be read.

home.description: The home directory of the terminal's program. Empty if the server can't tell.

status.description: Whether the directory could be read: 'ok', 'missing' (it doesn't exist), 'not_dir' (it, or a directory on its path, isn't a directory), or 'denied' (the server isn't allowed to read it).

name.description: The entry's name within the directory.

symlink.description: True if the entry is a symbolic link. A link that leads nowhere is left out of the listing.

file.description: True if the entry isn't a directory, or is a link to something that isn't. Only set when the request sets files.

entries.description: The matching entries, hidden ones included, in the order the filesystem returns them. Sorting and hiding are up to the client. Empty unless status is 'ok'.

truncated.description: True if some matching entries were left out because the listing reached limit or grew too large for one reply. To see the rest, list again with a prefix.

methods.name: modes
methods.description: List the terminal modes that programs can turn on, such as the alternate screen, bracketed paste, and mouse reporting, with each mode's name, number, and whether it is on. It doesn't wake an idle terminal.

screen.description: Which screen the terminal shows: 'primary', or 'alternate' while a full-screen program such as an editor has switched to it with mode 47, 1047, or 1049. Treat any other value as 'primary'.

name.description: The mode's name, as Ghostty names it, such as 'bracketed_paste' or 'alt_screen_save_cursor_clear_enter'.

number.description: The number a program sends to set or reset the mode, such as 2004 for bracketed paste.

ansi.description: True for an ANSI mode, which a program sets with ESC [ number h. Left out for a DEC private mode, which a program sets with ESC [ ? number h. The two kinds are numbered separately, so the same number can name one mode of each kind.

set.description: True if the mode is on.

default.description: True if the mode is on in a new terminal and after a reset. Left out if it is off. A mode whose set differs from its default was changed by a program.

modes.description: Every mode the terminal tracks, ANSI modes first, each group by number. Newer servers can add modes, so look modes up by name or number and skip any you don't know.

methods.name: ports
methods.description: List the TCP ports that programs in the terminal are listening on, such as a development server's, with each port's address and the process that holds it. status is 'partial' when some processes couldn't be looked at, so a port missing from a partial reply may still be open. A truncated reply has an id, and blob_read with that id returns the whole list. It doesn't wake an idle terminal. To follow changes, call it once and then follow the ports_changed event.

status.description: How complete ports is: 'ok' if every process in the terminal was looked at, 'partial' if some could not be, so ports may be missing some, or 'unsupported' if this server cannot list ports for this terminal. Treat any other value as 'partial'.

address.description: The address the socket is bound to, as an IP literal with no brackets, such as 127.0.0.1, ::1, 0.0.0.0, or ::. An IPv4 address mapped into IPv6 is given as plain IPv4. An IPv6 link-local address keeps its zone, an interface index, as in fe80::1%1.

protocol.description: The transport protocol, 'tcp' today. Skip an entry whose protocol you don't know.

first_seen_at.description: When the server first saw this address and port held by this process in this terminal, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. The server looks in the background, every second while there is output or input in any terminal and every 5 minutes at most while nothing happens, and also when asked, so this can be minutes after the port opened. It changes if the port closes and opens again or another process holds it.

pid.description: The ID of the process that holds the socket, or the first started of several that share it. The process is described by the entry in processes with the same pid. Left out when the server can't tell which process holds the socket, such as a server started with sudo, and the reply is then partial.

ports.description: The ports that programs in the terminal listen on, sorted by port and then by address, with one entry for each protocol, address and port. An empty array when nothing is listening.

user_id.description: The user ID the process runs as on Unix, which shows when a command runs as another user, such as with sudo. Zero on Windows.

user.description: The name of the account the process runs as. Left out if it can't be looked up.

name.description: The file name of the executable, such as zsh. When path is left out, the system's own name for the process, which Linux limits to 15 bytes. To label a process, use the first of script, argv0, and name that is present.

path.description: The absolute path of the executable, with symlinks resolved. Left out if it can't be read, as for another user's process on Linux.

invoked_path.description: The absolute path the executable was started through, before symlinks were resolved, such as a link in a bin directory. Present only when Rex can confirm it leads to the same file as path.

argv0.description: The first argument as the process shows it now, such as -zsh for a login shell, cut to 256 bytes. Rex never returns the other arguments, because they can hold secrets.

script.description: For an interpreter such as node or python, the absolute path of the script it is running, as the user named it. Left out for other programs.

cwd.description: The process's working directory, as an absolute path. Left out if it can't be read, as for another user's process.

processes.description: The processes that hold the ports, sorted by pid, with one entry for each, described as the process method describes them. A pid in ports with no entry here is a process the server couldn't describe. Each is described when its first port is found, so fields such as cwd show their value from then.

truncated.description: True if entries were left out from the end of ports so that the reply fits in one message. processes then describes only the processes that the remaining entries name. Left out when false.

id.description: Set only when truncated is true. Names a stored copy of the whole reply, from the same scan. Read it with blob_read from offset 0 until eof, and decode the text as a ports reply. The server keeps it for a few minutes. Left out if the server couldn't store the copy.

methods.name: process
methods.description: Get the processes running in the terminal and how its program exited.

exit_code.description: The program's exit code, or -1 if it has none, as when a signal ended it.

error.description: Why the program failed, such as 'exit status 1'. Left out when it exited successfully.

last_exit.description: How the terminal's program exited. Null while it is still running, and for a terminal that didn't start a program of its own.

user_id.description: The user ID the process runs as on Unix, which shows when a command runs as another user, such as with sudo. Zero on Windows.

user.description: The name of the account the process runs as. Left out if it can't be looked up.

name.description: The file name of the executable, such as zsh. When path is left out, the system's own name for the process, which Linux limits to 15 bytes. To label a process, use the first of script, argv0, and name that is present.

path.description: The absolute path of the executable, with symlinks resolved. Left out if it can't be read, as for another user's process on Linux.

invoked_path.description: The absolute path the executable was started through, before symlinks were resolved, such as a link in a bin directory. Present only when Rex can confirm it leads to the same file as path.

argv0.description: The first argument as the process shows it now, such as -zsh for a login shell, cut to 256 bytes. Rex never returns the other arguments, because they can hold secrets.

script.description: For an interpreter such as node or python, the absolute path of the script it is running, as the user named it. Left out for other programs.

cwd.description: The process's working directory, as an absolute path. Left out if it can't be read, as for another user's process.

child.description: The process the terminal started, usually a shell. On macOS a login shell runs under login, and this describes login. Left out if there is no such process or it can't be read.

user_id.description: The user ID the process runs as on Unix, which shows when a command runs as another user, such as with sudo. Zero on Windows.

user.description: The name of the account the process runs as. Left out if it can't be looked up.

name.description: The file name of the executable, such as zsh. When path is left out, the system's own name for the process, which Linux limits to 15 bytes. To label a process, use the first of script, argv0, and name that is present.

path.description: The absolute path of the executable, with symlinks resolved. Left out if it can't be read, as for another user's process on Linux.

foreground.description: The process in the foreground, such as the shell at its prompt or the command it is running. For a wrapper such as sudo, git, or cargo, it is the command the wrapper runs. Left out if it can't be found or read.

script.description: For an interpreter such as node or python, the absolute path of the script it is running, as the user named it. Left out for other programs.

cwd.description: The process's working directory, as an absolute path. Left out if it can't be read, as for another user's process.

ancestors.description: The processes between foreground and child, nearest first: the parent of foreground, then its parent, and so on, ending with child. Left out when foreground is child, when there are more than 16, or when one of them has exited.

home.description: The home directory that the terminal's program inherited, for showing and expanding ~ in paths.

methods.name: program_status
methods.description: List the status that programs in the terminal have reported. Programs report a status, such as working or blocked, with OSC 7501 escape sequences.

id.description: The record's ID. A slash separates a parent from a child, as in build/test. Left out for the root record, which holds the reports that give no ID.

state.description: What the program says it is doing: 'idle', 'working', 'done', 'blocked' (waiting for the user), or 'error'. Treat a value you don't know as 'idle'.

kind.description: What a blocked program is waiting for: 'permission', 'question', or 'auth' (a password or other credential). Left out if the program didn't say. Treat a value you don't know as if it were left out.

progress.description: How far along the program is, as a percentage from 0 to 100. Only working and blocked records have one, and only if the program reported it.

app.description: The program's name, such as cargo or terraform, exactly as it reported it.

effective_app.description: The name of the program the record belongs to: app if it is set, or else the app of the nearest parent record that has one. Left out if no record in the chain has an app.

title.description: A short label for the record, such as the name of a task. It comes from the program, so show it as plain text.

msg.description: One line of text describing the status. Show it as plain text. A client may shorten it but shouldn't try to interpret it.

updated_at.description: When the report arrived, by the server's clock, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

name.description: The process's name, found the same way as name in the result of process. Compare it as well as pid, because the system reuses process IDs.

owner.description: The terminal's foreground process when the report arrived. Left out if the server couldn't tell.

records.description: Every record, sorted by id. The root record comes first, and each parent comes before its children. Empty if no program has reported a status.

methods.name: pwd
methods.description: Get the working directory that a program in the terminal last reported. To find where each process actually is, call process instead.

pwd.description: The reported directory: a file:// URL when the program used OSC 7, or a plain path otherwise. Left out if no directory has been reported or a reset cleared it.

name.description: The process's name, found the same way as name in the result of process. Compare it as well as pid, because the system reuses process IDs.

owner.description: The process that reported the directory. Left out if pwd is left out or the server couldn't tell.

methods.name: reset
methods.description: Reset the terminal to its starting state and clear the screen and scrollback. The program keeps running, and the size and default colors stay the same.

methods.name: resize
methods.description: Request a terminal size in columns and rows. It applies at once if the caller owns the block or no client does, and otherwise when the caller becomes the owner.

columns.description: The width in columns, that is, characters per line, from 1 to 65535.

rows.description: The height in rows, from 1 to 65535.

cell_width_px.description: The width of one character cell in pixels, from 1 to 65535. Send it together with cell_height_px, or leave both out to keep the current cell size.

cell_height_px.description: The height of one character cell in pixels, from 1 to 65535. Send it together with cell_width_px, or leave both out to keep the current cell size.

methods.name: set_theme
methods.description: Replace the terminal's default colors. As with resize, they apply at once if the caller owns the block or no client does, and otherwise when the caller becomes the owner.

foreground.description: The default text color, as hex RRGGBB or #RRGGBB, such as #d6deeb. Empty or left out uses the built-in color.

background.description: The default background color, as hex RRGGBB or #RRGGBB, such as #011627. Empty or left out uses the built-in color.

cursor.description: The cursor color, as hex RRGGBB or #RRGGBB, such as #80a4c2. Empty or left out uses the built-in color.

palette.description: Changes to the 256-color palette, each written as index=RRGGBB or index=#RRGGBB with an index from 0 to 255, such as 1=#ef5350. Colors not listed keep their built-in values.

scheme.description: Whether the theme is 'light' or 'dark', which programs in the terminal can ask for. If empty, the terminal decides from how bright background is, and treats no background as dark.

methods.name: size
methods.description: Get the terminal's size, its owner, and the size each client last requested.

cell_width_px.description: The width of one character cell in pixels.

cell_height_px.description: The height of one character cell in pixels.

owner.description: The client that owns the block, whose size the terminal uses. Null if the block has no owner.

client_id.description: The client that requested this size.

updated_at.description: When the server received the request, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

desired.description: The last size each client requested, the owner's included, newest first.

methods.name: title
methods.description: Get the terminal's title and the process that set it.

title.description: The terminal's title, as a program last set it. Empty if no title is set.

name.description: The process's name, found the same way as name in the result of process. Compare it as well as pid, because the system reuses process IDs.

owner.description: The process that set the title, as title_changed reported it. Left out if no title is set, a reset cleared it, or the server couldn't tell.

methods.name: upload_begin
methods.description: Reserve a file to upload to the terminal's machine, such as one the user dropped on the terminal, and get a ticket for the rex.data.bytes.v1 data stream that carries its bytes. Once every file of the batch has arrived, the terminal types their paths as if the user had pasted them.

ref.description: The data reference for the file's stream: upload: followed by a new UUID in lower-case canonical form, which the client chooses.

name.description: The file's name. Only its last path component is used, without control characters.

size.description: The file's exact size in bytes.

batch.description: An ID the client chooses for a group of files whose paths are typed together. Left out, the file is uploaded on its own.

index.description: The file's position in its batch, from 0. Paths are typed in this order.

count.description: How many files the batch has. Required with batch.

ticket.description: A single-use ticket to send in the HELLO message that opens the data connection. Only a data connection from the same user can use it.

expires_in_ms.description: How long the ticket stays valid after the server issues it, in milliseconds.

methods.name: write
methods.description: Type text into the terminal as if the user had typed it. The call returns once the text is queued, without waiting for the program to read it.

data.description: The text to type. It can hold escape sequences for keys that aren't text, such as \u001b[A for the up arrow.

bytes_written.description: The number of bytes queued, which is the length of data in UTF-8 bytes, not characters.

methods.name: info
methods.description: Return what the tunnel forwards and how many connections it is relaying.

flavor.description: How the tunnel runs: dial or listen.

target.description: For a dial tunnel, the host and port it connects to. Left out for a listen tunnel.

address.description: For a listen tunnel, the IP address and port it listens on, including the port it picked if it was asked for port 0. Left out for a dial tunnel.

client_address.description: For a dial tunnel, where the owner said it listens, if it said. Left out for a listen tunnel.

client_target.description: For a listen tunnel, where the owner said it connects to, if it said. Left out for a dial tunnel.

last_owner.description: The client that owned the tunnel most recently. It stays set after the tunnel loses its owner, as it does as soon as the owner's connection drops, so it can be the owner of a tunnel that has none now. Left out if the tunnel has had no owner since it was created or restored.

connections.description: How many connections the tunnel is relaying now.
